newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- The national housing ministry is to take effective control of the Eastern Cape's housing department which sources described as being "in a complete shambles".

- Finance Minister Trevor Manuel is expected to unveil a budget on Tuesday which will slash spending to achieve a deficit of four percent of GDP or about R25 billion, as well as moves to ease exchange controls.

- The financial markets were in a cautiously optimistic mood ahead of expectations that Finance Minister Trevor Manuel would deliver a fiscally sound budget and make a move towards removing exchange controls.
- Money invested by members of the "pyramid-style money making scheme" Newport plc was collected around South Africa on Sunday and flown to Amsterdam, the High Court heard on Tuesday.

- Former foreign affairs minister Pik Botha probably knew and certainly lied to the Botswana government about a botched security police car bomb operation in 1987 aimed at African National Congress (ANC) activists, the truth commission's amnesty committee heard.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Budget-watchers are expecting Trevor Manuel to table a "please all, friendly" budget in parliament. The only groups that may feel dissatisfied are organised labour and the super-rich, they said.
- Labour Minister Tito Mboweni expressed sympathy and understanding on Tuesday for unions that wanted to stay racially exclusive after meeting the white Mine Workers' Union.
- Positive expectations of the budget fuelled another fine day on the JSE on Tuesday, dealers said, as the all share index gained a percent to 7,162 points and gold recovered.

- The government and trade unions representing the telecommunications industry are set to establish a development trust which could receive a "significant portion" of Telkom's estimated two billion rand black empowerment stake, industry sources said.
SAKE BEELD
- The government is considering a review of laws on property rent to provide greater protection to tenants being exploited by owners.
- AECI attributable earnings for the year to December end increased eight percent to R426 million.

- A panel of analysts from Old Mutual say Trevor Manuel's budget will hold few surprises but tax-watchers say it might be seen as the "budget of lost opportunities" if there is no increase in the Value Added Tax rate.
THE STAR
- Rain caused havoc to greater Johannesburg, damaging property and disrupting postal and telephone services.
- The rain has flooded hordes of underground ant colonies, forcing them to seek food inside homes.
- A teenage girl burnt to death after a truck rammed into the car she was in during a massive pile-up in bad weather near Shongweni on the N3.
- Rescue teams recovered the body of flood victim Jean Roussouw nearly 50 km from the bridge his car was swept off a week ago.
- About 20,000 Zulu marchers are expected to converge on the Johannesburg city centre to commemorate the 1994 Shell House massacre and to call for the day to be declared a public holiday.
